display.purpose: Red Hat Display 800. The one page headline; the closing section of the home page repeats the size.

band-title.purpose: Red Hat Display 800. The smaller headline cut that titles the bands of the course page.

row-title.purpose: Red Hat Display 700. Project row titles, the dock title and footer link names.

subhead.purpose: Red Hat Display 700. Subheads inside the bands of the course page.

name.purpose: Red Hat Display 700. The name of a service on the board; the site name in the bar uses the size at 800.

lede.purpose: Red Hat Text 400. The one paragraph under a headline, at most 31em wide.

body.purpose: Red Hat Text 400. Running text, capped between 34em and 36em.

small.purpose: Red Hat Text 400. Service descriptions, notes and the small print of the footer.

button.purpose: Red Hat Text 650. Action text; 1rem in the small button, up to 1.25rem in the large one.

label.purpose: Red Hat Mono 500, uppercase, tracked, muted. The board header, terms in a term list and chapter ranges.

pill.purpose: Red Hat Mono 600, sentence case. The text of a state pill.

mono.purpose: Red Hat Mono 500. Repository names, and literal identifiers inside a sentence at 0.92em.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing token (--ease). Every transition and the animations of the board use it. The two scroll-driven effects are linear, and the circuit traces keep slower curves of their own.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover changes of fill, border and underline colour on buttons (the primary button mixes 14% of the ground into its fill), navigation links, the theme switch, board rows and text links. Kept under reduced motion.

motion.name: icon-nudge
motion.value: transform 220ms; translate(2px, -2px) for a diagonal arrow, 3px along the axis for the others
motion.purpose: The icon after a link, and the arrow after a board row name, moves in the direction it points on hover. Removed under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, together with the 1px pressed shift of a button.

motion.name: check-in
motion.value: 420ms, fill backwards; delays 350ms, 600ms, 850ms per row; indicator from opacity 0.15 and scale 0.4, pill from opacity 0 and translateX(8px)
motion.purpose: On load each board row checks in: its indicator fills and its pill arrives, one row after another. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: pulse
motion.value: 2.6s, infinite, after 1.5s; scale 1 to 3.4, opacity 0.45 to 0
motion.purpose: A slow ring around the indicator of the one service on a board that is open right now. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: signal
motion.value: 7s, infinite, cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.3, 1); stroke-dashoffset 6 to -100 over the first 45%; delays 0s, 1.3s, 2.9s, 4.1s, 5.2s
motion.purpose: Ember dashes travel down five of the circuit traces towards the home board. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; otherwise the dashes are not drawn.

motion.name: spark
motion.value: 3.6s, infinite, ease-in-out; opacity 0.35 to 1 and back; delays 0s, 1.2s, 2.1s
motion.purpose: Three ember sparks at the nodes of the circuit traces fade and return. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; otherwise they stay at full strength.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% entry 60%; from opacity 0 and translateY(14px)
motion.purpose: Project rows rise and fade in as they enter the screen, where scroll-driven animation is supported. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: bar-line
motion.value: animation-timeline: scroll(); animation-range: 0 64px; border-bottom-color from transparent to --line
motion.purpose: The pinned bar gains its bottom hairline over the first 64px of scroll. Where scroll-driven animation is not supported the hairline is always drawn.

motion.name: theme-reveal
motion.value: 560ms; clip-path: circle(0) to circle(150vmax) at the centre of the theme switch (--vt-x, --vt-y)
motion.purpose: Changing theme opens the new theme as a circle from the switch, through a view transition. Skipped under reduced motion and where view transitions are missing.

motion.name: page-transition
motion.value: @view-transition { navigation: auto }; named groups: bar, course-title
motion.purpose: Moving between the home page and the course page keeps the bar in place and morphs the course name into the headline of the course page. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

components.name: Circuit Traces
components.description: The forge, home page only: hairline circuit traces that end on the top edge of the service board, with ring nodes, ember signals that travel down five traces and three ember sparks. With the mark, the only place ember appears. Decoration: hidden from assistive technology, shown from 1000px, removed in print; without motion the signals are not drawn and the sparks stay still.

components.css: .ds-spec { max-width: 26rem; margin: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); color: var(--ink); font-family: var(--text); font-size: 1.0625rem; } .ds-spec > div { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 7rem minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 16px; padding: 12px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); } .ds-spec dt { padding-top: 3px; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--mute); } .ds-spec dd { margin: 0; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; line-height: 1.4; }

components.name: Dock
components.description: The one panel that stays dark in both themes. It holds the third-party waiting list form, which has light text, and a plain link that opens the same form in a new tab. Selection and the focus ring inside it take the dock text colour.
components.html:
Join the waitlist

Open the form in a new tab
components.css: .ds-dock { max-width: 30rem; padding: 24px 20px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--dock-line); border-radius: 12px; background: var(--dock); color: var(--dock-ink); font-family: var(--text); line-height: 1.55; } .ds-dock ::selection { background: var(--dock-ink); color: var(--dock); } .ds-dock :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--dock-ink); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-dock__title { margin: 0 8px; font-family: var(--display); font-size: clamp(1.25rem, 1.1rem + 0.6vw, 1.5rem); font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: -0.016em; } .ds-dock__alt { margin: 16px 8px 12px; font-size: 0.9375rem; } .ds-link { color: inherit; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 1.5px; text-decoration-color: var(--line-strong); text-underline-offset: 0.2em; transition: text-decoration-color 160ms var(--ease); } .ds-link:hover { text-decoration-color: currentcolor; }

components.name: Footer Link
components.description: A title-sized name with a direction icon and one muted line under it. The footer sets them two across, then four from 900px. On hover only the icon moves.
components.html: BlogTutorials and guides
components.css: .ds-uplink { display: block; color: var(--ink); font-family: var(--text); font-size: 1.0625rem; line-height: 1.55; text-decoration: none; } .ds-uplink:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-uplink__name { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 32px; font-family: var(--display); font-size: clamp(1.25rem, 1.1rem + 0.6vw, 1.5rem); font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: -0.016em; } .ds-uplink__desc { display: block; color: var(--mute); } .ds-ico { flex: none; width: 1em; height: 1em; fill: none; stroke: currentcolor; stroke-width: 1.75; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; transition: transform 220ms var(--ease); } .ds-btn:hover > .ds-ico--ext, .ds-link:hover > .ds-ico--ext, .ds-uplink:hover .ds-ico--ext { transform: translate(2px, -2px); } .ds-btn:hover > .ds-ico--down { transform: translateY(3px); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-ico { transition: none; } :is(.ds-btn, .ds-link, .ds-uplink, .ds-svc, .ds-nav a):hover .ds-ico { transform: none; } .ds-btn:active { transform: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The site reads as the status board of a small infrastructure practice. Every page opens with one bordered board that lists what is on offer as services. Each row is a link and carries an indicator, a name with an arrow, one line of description and, on most rows, a state pill. The board is the proof, the in-page navigation and the first thing a visitor reads.

The system is restrained and neutral. It ships two themes of equal standing, dark and light, with the same roles. The page follows the system setting and remembers a manual choice made with a visible switch. Grounds are near-neutral with a slight green cast, structure is drawn in one-pixel hairlines, and nothing casts a shadow. Hue appears only as state: green for what is live, amber for what is coming, neutral for what is not available. The one exception is the forge: ember orange, the brand colour, on the mark and on the circuit traces above the home board, approved by the owner. A drenched multi-colour direction was built first and rejected by the owner as too colourful; this system replaces it.

Three Red Hat typefaces split the work: one for headings and names, one for reading and controls, one for labels, states and literal identifiers. Motion is tied to the board: on the home page ember signals travel down the traces into it, its indicators check in on load, the local time and the last push are live data, and changing theme is a circular reveal from the switch.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes of equal standing with identical roles; every colour is read through a custom property.
Hue as state: green, amber or neutral. Everything else is ink, muted ink and hairlines.
Ember, the brand colour, only on the forge: the mark and the circuit traces.
State labels from a closed set of six.
One bordered board per page, with rows as links.
One-pixel hairlines and rows instead of cards.
No shadows, no gradients, no blur.
Three Red Hat typefaces with fixed jobs.
Gently rounded controls (`8px`), panels (`12px`) and full pills for states.
Authored animation only when the reader has not asked for reduced motion.

rules.name: The State Only Rule
rules.body: Outside the forge, hue says what state something is in and does nothing else. Green is live, amber is coming, neutral is not available. No heading, link, button or surface carries a hue.

rules.name: The Forge Rule
rules.body: Ember is the brand colour and belongs to the forge alone: the ground of the mark, and the signals and sparks of the circuit traces. It is the one exception to the State Only Rule, approved by the owner. Ember never sets text, never fills a button, a pill or a surface, and never stands for a state.

rules.name: The Closed Set Rule
rules.body: A state is named with one of six labels. Green: Available, Public, Open. Amber: Coming soon. Neutral: Private, Offline.

rules.name: The Tint Pair Rule
rules.body: A state colour sets text only on its own tint, as a pill. On any other ground it appears only as a `10px` indicator.

rules.name: The Shared Roles Rule
rules.body: Components name roles, never literal colours. Both themes define every role, so a component is written once and the theme switch never touches it. The one literal in the build is the lettering of the mark, which is the same dark in both themes.

rules.name: The Three Faces Rule
rules.body: Display sets headings and names. Text sets reading and controls. Mono sets labels, states and literal identifiers. A face is never borrowed for another job.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: Display appears at 800 for the site name and the headings of a page and its sections, and at 700 for titles and names inside them.

rules.name: The Capitals Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with tracking belongs to the mono label alone. It captions data: a board header, a term, a range.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: A surface is a panel tone and a hairline. Nothing floats and nothing casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with one-pixel lines. Thickness is never used for emphasis.

rules.name: The Shape Scale Rule
rules.body: `8px` for a control, `12px` for a panel, a full pill for a state, a circle for an indicator. A focus ring follows the shape it sits in.

rules.name: The One Board Rule
rules.body: A page has one board. The dock is the only other bordered panel, and it exists to hold a third-party form. Everything else is rows between hairlines.

rules.name: The True State Rule
rules.body: An indicator or a pill states something that is true today. Live detail always has a plain text fallback in the markup.

rules.name: The Quiet Motion Rule
rules.body: One easing curve, `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, drives every transition and the animations of the board; the traces keep slower curves of their own. The check-in, the pulse, the signals, the sparks, the settle, the theme reveal and the page transition run only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the icon movement on hover and the pressed shift of a button are removed as well, and only colour transitions remain.

dos: Do read every colour from a role (`--bg`, `--panel`, `--ink`, `--mute`, `--line`, `--line-strong` and the state pairs), so both themes follow.
Do use green, amber and neutral only to state what is live, what is coming and what is not available.
Do put state colour on its own tint as a pill, or alone as a `10px` indicator.
Do keep ember to the forge: the ground of the mark, and the signals and sparks of the circuit traces.
Do name a state with one of the six labels: Available, Public, Open, Coming soon, Private, Offline.
Do open a page with one board whose rows are links and whose states are true today.
Do separate repeated content with one-pixel hairlines and rows.
Do set headings and names in Red Hat Display at 800 or 700, reading text and controls in Red Hat Text, and labels, states and literal identifiers in Red Hat Mono.
Do keep text blocks to a measure between `31em` and `36em`.
Do use `8px` for controls, `12px` for panels and a full pill for states.
Do keep every button and every target in the bar at least `44px` tall; the standard button is `52px`.
Do give live detail a plain text fallback that is true without script.
Do gate authored animation behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, and remove movement on hover and on press under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
Do check both themes: text pairs measure at least `4.9:1` and the strong line at least `3:1`.
donts: Don't use hue as decoration outside the forge: no coloured headings, links, buttons, section fills or icons. A drenched multi-colour direction was built and rejected by the owner.
Don't use ember for text, for a button, for a pill, for a surface or for a state.
Don't write a literal colour in a component, and don't ship a component that works in one theme only. The dock is the one inverted surface, dark in both themes.
Don't add shadows, gradients or blur. The build has none.
Don't box repeated content into cards. The board and the dock are the only bordered panels.
Don't use line thickness for emphasis; rules and borders stay at one pixel.
Don't set uppercase or tracked text outside the mono label.
Don't use Red Hat Mono for headings or running text.
Don't show a state that is not true on the day it is published.
